connection_pool_saturation.title: DB Connection Pool Saturation
steps: Check DB connection count: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;
Identify long-running queries: SELECT pid, query, state, now()-query_start FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle';
Kill queries older than 30s if safe
Increase pool size: pool_size=100 → pool_size=200
Enable connection queue metrics and set alert threshold at 80%
Restart auth-service to release stale connections

memory_leak.title: Memory Leak / OOM
steps: Capture heap profile: curl /debug/pprof/heap > heap.out
Identify top allocators: go tool pprof -top heap.out
Restart affected pods to reclaim memory
Set memory limit and OOM killer alerts
File a bug with the heap profile attached
Deploy fix and monitor RSS for 24h

network_latency.title: Upstream Network Latency
steps: Confirm latency: ping/traceroute to upstream service
Check upstream service health dashboard
Verify DNS resolution time: dig upstream.service
Increase client timeout and add retry with jitter
Open circuit breaker if error rate > 10%
Notify upstream team if issue persists

third_party_outage.title: Third-Party Vendor Outage
steps: Check vendor status page and status webhook
Enable retry with exponential backoff
Failover to backup provider if available
Queue failed requests for replay
Notify customer support with estimated impact
Post-mortem once vendor recovers

auth_single_point_of_failure.title: Auth Service Cascade
steps: Verify auth-service health and pod count
Check for clock skew: date on each node vs NTP
Enable JWT validation cache with 5-min TTL
Add circuit breaker to auth calls with 200ms timeout
Deploy fallback auth for critical endpoints
Post-incident: shard auth or add read replica

bad_deploy_upstream_unavailable.title: Bad Deploy — Upstream Unavailable
steps: Rollback deploy immediately: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>
Verify pod health after rollback
Drain traffic from affected AZ if partial
Inspect deploy diff for breaking changes
Add readiness probe with proper warmup
Enforce canary deploy with automatic rollback

missing_index.title: Missing Database Index
steps: Identify slow query: pg_stat_statements ORDER BY total_time DESC
Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the slow query
Create index concurrently: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ...
Verify query plan uses new index
Monitor p99 latency for 1 hour
Document index and add to schema migration

replication_lag.title: DB Replication Lag
steps: Check replica lag: SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp();
Inspect replica IO and CPU
Route reads to primary temporarily
Check for long-running write on primary
Increase WAL sender/receiver buffers if needed
Rebuild replica from snapshot if lag persists > 10 min
